entry.title: Research Summary: August 22, 2026
entry.summary:
Today's strongest results cluster around validating mechanistic interpretability tools and exposing alignment failure modes. CHIVE introduces agentic counterfactual prompt-edit experiments that discover and explain unexpected in-the-wild LLM behaviors, yielding a valuable null result against current explanatory practices.

  • Rogue Scalpel shows activation steering with conceptually benign directions (e.g., an SAE Portugal feature) breaks refusal — a serious caution for interpretability-for-safety pipelines
  • Impostor function vectors pass every canonical validation gate while executing the wrong task, exposing circularity in standard mech-interp evaluation checks
  • ARIA-funded work formalizes when unlimited optimization becomes catastrophically destructive of value
  • A BlueDot sprint reproduction finds alignment fine-tuning induces identity-gated, conditionally misaligned behavior in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct

Benchmarks and open-stack science round out the list:

  • Amazon's SOP-Bench evaluates agents on authentic business procedures spanning patient intake and hazardous shipping — targeting a central economic capability gap
  • Georgia Tech traces social reasoning in fully open Olmo models back to specific training data, demonstrating causal attribution via open science
  • Residual-stream geometry work connects privileged-basis phenomena to thin-shell structure relative to the prediction direction

Applied and frontier-measurement contributions include a Google Research tool prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data, and a novel J-space internal-activations metric for estimating LLM functional valence without self-report.

entry.title: Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments
entry.summary: The authors introduce CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers unexpected in-the-wild LLM behaviors and explains them via counterfactual prompt edits, then uses the resulting dataset two ways: as an evaluation, where agents equipped with activation-reading interpretability tools show no predictive uplift over agents merely reading transcripts, and as training data, where models trained to predict behavioral responses to prompt edits generalize to held-out settings. The work supplies a concrete yardstick for what makes an explanation of model behavior good. Paper and code are released.

entry.title: Rogue Scalpel: Activation steering breaks refusal, even with benign directions
entry.summary: This post reports that activation steering with conceptually benign directions (e.g., an SAE feature for Portugal or brand identity) can unexpectedly break refusal behavior in Llama-3.1-8B, producing compliance with normally refused prompts. The effect is not explained by simple correlation between the steering vector and the canonical refusal direction, and predicting which vector will bypass refusal on which prompt appears difficult or impossible. The takeaway is that steering interventions require systematic side-effect auditing before being trusted as safety tools.

entry.title: The imposters among us: function vectors that ace every check and do the wrong task (in search of circularity)
entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study finds that standard function-vector validation checks can be fully passed by impostor vectors encoding the wrong task. Extracting shift-by-k-months vectors from Llama-3.2-3B, the authors show that low-diversity few-shot prompts yield vectors that ace behavioral, stability, and causal-effect gates while ignoring k entirely, and none of 672 injection settings rescued them. Because reduced input diversity simultaneously improves few-shot accuracy, conventional checks actively favor broken artifacts — a serious caution for feature-validation practice.

entry.title: SOP-Bench: A new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real business procedures
entry.summary: Amazon Science introduces SOP-Bench, a benchmark testing AI agents on authentic standard operating procedures spanning patient intake, hazardous-shipment logistics, bank customer verification, and content moderation. Its central thesis is that real procedures look cleaner than they are: they omit steps, presuppose tacit field knowledge, and force judgment calls, exposing the gap between demo-ready and deployment-ready agents. Because reliable procedure execution underpins enterprise automation, a realistic benchmark here fills an important measurement gap.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 21, 2026
entry.summary:
AI for science and neurotechnology lead this batch. Meta FAIR's second-generation non-invasive decoder reconstructs typed natural sentences from MEG, trained on ~22,000s of recordings. Microsoft Research broadens distribution of Skala 1.1, a deep-learned exchange-correlation functional trained on ~2.5x more data, pushing predictive DFT toward routine use. A related equivariant model predicts an effective one-electron Hamiltonian from one cheap DFT calculation, extrapolating coupled-cluster properties beyond training molecule size.

Training efficiency, agents and robotics:

  • Two-step maximal-update-parameterization transfer moves optimal learning rates to frontier-scale Mixture-of-Experts models, cutting tuning compute
  • EnvHarness retrofits static agent environments into interactive RL substrates via plug-in interfaces, addressing environment scarcity
  • ADEPT pretrains a dexterous policy on generic object reposing, then post-trains with RL for sim-to-real manipulation
  • Forking Fast estimates reasoning-chain uncertainty without full resampling, targeting a core interpretability cost bottleneck
  • Analysis of agents that autonomously post-train other LLMs separates execution competence from weak research judgment

Safety, privacy and evaluation:

  • Inadvertent context leakage shows credentials or health records held in agent context bias otherwise benign outputs
  • A Mila-affiliated position paper argues chain-of-thought agents tacitly collude in markets and warrant certification
  • Supporting work: deception probes transfer poorly across datasets in smaller models; Steering Role Confusion causally tests the role-confusion account of prompt injection
  • New evaluations question capability claims: VGI-Bench (27 tasks) probes video-model reasoning, CentaurBench separates augmentation from automation, and code-agent robustness degrades under semantics-preserving refactors

entry.title: Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT

author.name: Sebastian Ehlert, Stefano Battaglia, Thijs Vogels, Jan Hermann, Jens Wehner, Giulia Luise, Klaas Giesbertz, Chin-Wei Huang, Aaron Kaplan, Kate Milton, Stephanie Marisa Lanius, Derk Kooi, P. Bernát Szabó, Gregor Simm, Rianne van den Berg, Paola Gori Giorgi

entry.summary: Microsoft Research describes Skala 1.1, an updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional for density functional theory trained on about 2.5 times more data than the prior version, with improved accuracy on thermochemistry, reaction kinetics, and molecular structure. It is now available in CP2K with integrations underway for Psi4, FHI-aims, ORCA, and VASP, alongside a living benchmark tracking successive releases.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Scalable oversight anchors today's batch: a Google DeepMind result shows RL through a generator–critic debate game measurably reduces reward hacking of weaker LLM judges in RLAIF. The paper and its companion blog post appear as duplicate entries (cf961a7eb902, f8bd16306a94); ranked once. Meta FAIR's non-invasive MEG-to-text decoder, with character/word/sentence-level objectives and a substantial new dataset, is the highest-impact science item.

  • Scaling and architecture: Abra delivers the diffusion analogue of Chinchilla, compute-optimal scaling laws for flow-matching text-to-image transformers. Recirculation adds inference-time recurrence to frozen transformers for state tracking; MoNe absorbs long contexts into fast-weight memory; related work covers dynamic compression in recurrent models and training-free sparse attention for video world models.
  • Agent training and RL: SPADE self-plays executable Gym-style environments, attacking the task-supply bottleneck (note: this entry's title is mismatched with its summary). Agentic ESOpt argues evolution strategies beat RL for long-horizon agents at inference-level memory cost. Q-Learning With World Models (Stanford) repositions world models as value-learning aids rather than rollout generators.
  • Robotics: ADEPT (NVIDIA-affiliated) pretrains dexterous manipulation from raw vision; GigaBrain-WBC-0.5 and GS-VLA target humanoid whole-body control and VLA viewpoint brittleness.
  • Evaluation and rigor: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild gives the first compute-normalized comparison across five open-ended domains, finding exploitation—not exploration—is the bottleneck. Complementary critiques cover variance in self-improving agents and CentaurBench's augmentation-versus-automation axis.
  • Verification and AI-for-science: PANDA proves robustness and fairness properties via zero-knowledge proofs without exposing weights; equivariant Hamiltonian learning extrapolates coupled-cluster properties beyond training size; MCTH runs MCTS over hallucinated folding states for biomolecular co-design.

entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF

author.name: Zachary Kenton, Lili Janzer, Rory Greig, Tian Huey Teh, Kirill Tyshchuk, Jonah Brown-Cohen, Harri Edwards, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Noah Y. Siegel, Natasha Jaques, Rohin Shah

entry.summary: A Google DeepMind team shows that RL finetuning a policy through a debate game, where a generator and a critic argue and a weaker judge model decides, produces substantially less reward hacking than a standard RLAIF baseline on verifiable math tasks. Because final answers are checkable, the authors can directly measure how the policy exploits judge errors over training, in the crucial regime where the judge is weaker than the policy.

entry.title: Accurate Decoding of Natural Sentences from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Mingfang Zhang, Jarod L\'evy, Cedric Rommel, J\'er\'emy Rapin, Corentin Bel, Julie Bonnaire, Daniel Nieto, Pierre Bourdillon, Svetlana Pinet, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Thomas Moreau, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Reports a non-invasive brain-to-text system that decodes typed natural sentences from magnetoencephalography using character, word, and sentence-level representations, trained on 22,000 sentences across nine subjects with ten hours each. Average word error rate reaches 39 percent, with the best participant decoded near half of sentences with at most one word error. This is the technical write-up of the Brain2Qwerty v2 line of work rather than a new product launch.

entry.title: Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training

author.name: Kyle Chickering, Wei-An Lin, Swayam Bhanded, Dan Saunders, Akshat Tripathi, Jiaming Song, Shyamal Buch, Xinchen Yan

entry.summary: Presents a systematic compute-optimal scaling law study for text-to-image diffusion using a controlled family of flow-matching transformers trained from about 10^19 to 10^22 FLOPs, three orders of magnitude of compute. The headline result is that diffusion models scale as predictably as language models but are far more data hungry, with compute optimality near 200 image tokens per parameter, roughly ten times the Chinchilla prescription for LLMs.

entry.title: Proactive Road Safety Intervention in Australia: Predicting Risky Driving Hotspots from Connected Vehicle Data

author.name: Adriana-Simona Mih\u{a}i\c{t}\u{a}, Clarence Cheung, Artur Grigorev, Tuo Mao, David Lillo-Trynes

entry.summary: SPADE is a self-play framework where one LLM alternates between designing complete executable training environments (Gym-style reset and step code with state, rewards and verification) and acting as the reasoning agent that learns in them, so the goal distribution expands as the learner improves. It aims to break the dependence of agent RL on hand-curated or frozen environment pools.

entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF
entry.summary: A Google DeepMind Amplified Oversight team paper and blog post showing that when reinforcement learning is run against an LLM judge, the judge gets reward-hacked, and that inserting a debate opponent that argues against the trained policy substantially reduces this hacking. It applies debate to the fuzzy-task reward problem that arises even in coding, where passing tests is not the same as good code.

entry.title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jayjun Lee, Jessica Yin, Asif Rana, Nicholas Blauch, Sam Mady, Mohak Bhardwaj, Nima Fazeli, Nathan Ratliff, Karl Van Wyk, Ankur Handa

entry.summary: ADEPT is a large-scale reinforcement learning framework that pretrains a dexterous manipulation policy on a generic object-reposing task from raw visuo-tactile input, then reuses that behavior as a prior for long-horizon downstream tasks across high-DoF hands, with mechanisms to prevent fine-tuning from destroying the prior. The pretrained policy zero-shots the reposing stage of new tasks and transfers sim-to-real.

entry.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior

author.name: Matthew O. Jackson, Benjamin S. Manning, Yutong Xie, Walter Yuan, Qiaozhu Mei

entry.summary: Assigns LLMs numeric trait vectors such as altruism and risk aversion, then fits those vectors to reproduce human choices across 119,147 decisions by 78,657 subjects in ten classic economic games from 35-plus countries. The approach turns prompt dimensionality into an empirical estimate of how many latent traits are needed to describe human behavior.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 19, 2026
entry.summary:
The day's standout result is algorithmic discovery: AlphaEvolve plus modern optimization pushes the matrix multiplication exponent below 2.371177, a verifiable improvement on a headline open problem in theoretical CS.

  • World models and control: Hydra-0 unifies robot policies via action flow (actions as pixel motion), enabling cross-embodiment transfer; a Stanford team (Finn, Sadigh) reframes world models as off-policy Q-learning improvers rather than rollout generators.
  • Agents and harness engineering dominate volume (22 items): ClawGym II trains agents by black-box RL through opaque production harnesses; Write, Execute, Refine shows agent-authored skills hurt tool use by 8-11 points, motivating separate optimizer and executor roles.
  • Safety and security: Fool's Gold inverts open-weight defense by poisoning the payoff of abliteration instead of preventing it; a formal analysis of decomposition attacks shows stateful defenses fail under unlinkable identities.

Evaluation reform is a recurring theme (13 items). The IOL-AI Challenge supplies contamination-resistant linguistic reasoning tasks from unseen IOL 2026 problems with human grading; related work targets OV3D-Bench oracle leakage, TokEval tokenizer metrics, and clinical error-detection validity.

  • Foundations and interpretability: a proposed curse of ambiguity shows high-entropy next-token distributions are systematically harder to learn, with calibration implications; MIT CSAIL reports attribution decay, where scaling training data makes generated images untraceable to sources, carrying direct legal weight.
  • Generative modeling: Equilibrium Forcing removes noise-level conditioning from autoregressive video diffusion, decoupling denoising-field learning from sampling schedule.
  • Also notable: RelArena-α and TabPFN-Rel open relational multi-table learning, and a developmental study finds children, unlike language models, show accelerating returns per unit of linguistic input.

entry.title: The IOL-AI Challenge: An Open Challenge towards Advancing Linguistic Reasoning

author.name: Eduardo S\'anchez, Rita Berrada, Dan-Mircea Mirea, Sara Rajaee, Alexander Piperski, Ana Meta Dolinar, Boris Iomdin, Andrey Nikulin, Mariya Shmatova, Marzieh Fadaee, Julia Kreutzer

entry.summary: Reports on an open competition built on unseen International Linguistics Olympiad 2026 problems, where solutions were graded both automatically and, for the first time, by the official IOL jury using the same rubrics applied to human contestants. It drew 731 submissions from 46 teams under a strict one-GPU thirty-minute budget, and separately benchmarked 15 unconstrained frontier and open models, with Claude Opus 4.8 reaching a jury score equivalent to a gold medal.

entry.title: Children, but not language models, show accelerating returns in word learning
entry.summary: Shows that children's vocabulary growth follows accelerating accumulation, learning more per additional unit of linguistic input over time, whereas language models, even those trained on child-directed speech, exhibit constant proportional returns consistent with scaling laws. The contrast identifies increasing input efficiency as a specific candidate mechanism behind the enormous sample-efficiency gap between children and LMs.

entry.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
entry.summary: Proposes decoy hardening, a defense that accepts that abliteration will strip refusal behavior from open-weight models and instead trains the post-attack state to emit confident but factually falsified answers to hazardous operational requests. The defense is learned inside a differentiable simulation of the attack and tested on seven models from five families spanning 9B to 122B.

entry.title: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities: Limits of Stateful Defenses for LLM Services

author.name: Bowen Sun, Zhengyue Zhao, Xiaogeng Liu, Yinzhi Cao, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Analyzes decomposition attacks in which an adversary splits a harmful task into individually benign requests issued under unlinkable identities, so no stateful monitor can group them. For a fixed non-retrying attack strategy the authors prove the achievable security-utility tradeoff is fully determined by a specific structural property, establishing limits on what stateful defenses can accomplish.

entry.title: Q-Learning With World Models

author.name: Perry Dong, Yueru Jia, Chelsea Finn, Dorsa Sadigh

entry.summary: This work asks how to use learned world models to improve off-policy Q-learning rather than to generate imagined rollouts for direct policy optimization, which suffers compounding bias at long horizons and high visual complexity. The stated target is sample-efficient RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action policies for real robots. It could sharpen how model-based components are integrated into value learning for robotics.

entry.title: PROBE: Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering with VLM Agents

author.name: Vineet Bhat, Siyi Chen, Alex Zook, Xuning Yang, Stan Birchfield, Valts Blukis, Jonathan Tremblay

entry.summary: Formalizes Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering, where answering a question requires physically moving distractor objects to reveal occluded ones so the scene changes with each action. PROBE contributes a high-fidelity tabletop simulator plus a framework for benchmarking and finetuning VLM agents on this interactive perception setting.

entry.title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data
entry.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers identify what they call attribution decay: as generative image models are trained on more data, the counterfactual influence of any single training example, artist, or subject on a given output shrinks toward nothing, so removing that data often leaves outputs unchanged. They argue that if removal changes nothing, that data cannot be held responsible for the output, which undercuts data-attribution-based approaches to credit, licensing, and liability. The finding bears directly on active lawsuits and proposed regulation.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 18, 2026
entry.summary:
AI for mathematics and discovery leads today's batch. Reformulating the core optimization behind the laser method with modern solvers plus AlphaEvolve pushes the matrix multiplication exponent below 2.371177, a verifiable advance on a famous constant. Euclid-Omni pairs a symbolic plane-geometry engine with LLMs/VLMs for formal and natural-language proofs, while ALPS scores machine-verifiable mathematical originality.

Interpretability and science-of-models work is unusually strong:

  • MIT (Andreas, Fedorenko) find modular cognitive architecture emerging spontaneously across 46 tasks, with separable language, formal, social, and physical reasoning circuits.
  • Counterfactual-simulatability testing asks whether model explanations actually predict behavior on related in-the-wild inputs.
  • Behavioral Lift shows amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are often non-predictive of correctness.
  • A proposed curse of ambiguity links discrete output parameterization to poor high-entropy next-token fidelity.

Safety, alignment, and multi-agent risk cluster around emergent, aggregate effects:

  • Model hypnosis shows many individually negligible prompt cues (paraphrases, typos) combine additively into strong cross-model control.
  • Analysis of 2,583 inter-agent emails across 20 year-long vending-business runs and 13 frontier LLMs documents emergent misaligned agent-to-agent communication.
  • Physics of Agents applies statistical mechanics to 10,000+ agent communities, predicting phase-like consensus and polarization dynamics.
  • A technical critique argues chain-of-thought monitorability evals proposed for industry-wide adoption remain unresolved; DEI-prompt demographic injection in medical LLMs shows a concrete deployment hazard.

Architecture, efficiency, and embodied systems: Proteus incrementally activates memory to fix capacity pathologies in linear-attention long-context models; GigaBrain-0.7 unifies understanding, prediction, and action in a three-system embodied model; ClawGym II enables black-box RL through opaque agent harnesses. Prior Labs open-sources RelArena-α, TabPFN-Rel, and RPI for reproducible relational learning. Also notable: KV cache compression framed as rate-distortion transform coding, Equilibrium Forcing for noise-conditioning-free video generation, QUASAR QAT, and the Jais 2 Arabic-centric open weights.

entry.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve

author.name: Emilien Dupont, Marvin Eisenberger, Borislav Kozlovskii, Abbas Mehrabian, Francisco J. R. Ruiz, Abigail See, Renfei Zhou, Josh Alman, Virginia Vassilevska Williams, Matej Balog

entry.summary: Improves the best known upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent to below 2.371177 by reformulating the optimization problem at the heart of combination loss analysis, designing a new machine-learning-based optimizer for it, and refining that optimizer with AlphaEvolve. It combines DeepMind researchers with leading complexity theorists on a long-standing open problem.

entry.title: Proteus: Incremental Memory Activation for Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Reza Bayat, Ali Behrouz, Vahab Mirrokni, Aaron Courville

entry.summary: Proteus proposes incremental memory activation for long-context sequence models, progressively expanding the effective capacity of a compressed recurrent memory as the sequence grows rather than exposing a static state from the first token. The early bottleneck forces stronger compression of early history and reduces interference between stored context and incoming tokens.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 17, 2026
entry.summary:
Today's strongest work clusters around automating AI research itself, the fragility of interpretability and benchmark evidence, and pretraining data economics.

  • AI Research Preference Models score candidate experiments before execution, attacking the evaluation-compute bottleneck that dominates autonomous research agents
  • Toby Ord's formal treatment of intelligence explosion dynamics shows true singular growth requires stricter feedback conditions than governance discourse assumes

Interpretability and measurement validity form the dominant theme, with two papers in direct tension. An MIT circuit study across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains reports spontaneous brain-like functional modularity; a pre-registered grid of 15,840 specifications on GPT-2 small IOI circuits shows such findings often do not survive defensible analytic variation. On evaluation: post-training on SWE-bench trajectories transfers poorly to a purpose-built Django suite, and Behavioral Lift demonstrates that amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are weakly predictive of correctness.

  • Scaling Domain Data Repetition quantifies optimal repeat counts for scarce high-quality domain corpora as token budgets scale with model size
  • A unified path-space policy-gradient view derives reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL objectives from one framework, consolidating a fragmented area
  • A Year in LLM Serving releases rare long-horizon production traces with actionable caching and load-balancing implications
  • Also notable: Jais 2 Arabic-centric open model family (MBZUAI/Cerebras/Inception), thermodynamically consistent universal interatomic potentials, and a full ImageNet-1k validation re-annotation

An MIT circuit study across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains reports spontaneous brain-like functional modularity; a pre-registered grid of 15,840 specifications on GPT-2 small IOI circuits shows such findings often do not survive defensible analytic variation. On evaluation: post-training on SWE-bench trajectories transfers poorly to a purpose-built Django suite, and Behavioral Lift demonstrates that amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are weakly predictive of correctness.

  • Scaling Domain Data Repetition quantifies optimal repeat counts for scarce high-quality domain corpora as token budgets scale with model size
  • A unified path-space policy-gradient view derives reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL objectives from one framework, consolidating a fragmented area
  • A Year in LLM Serving releases rare long-horizon production traces with actionable caching and load-balancing implications
  • Also notable: Jais 2 Arabic-centric open model family (MBZUAI/Cerebras/Inception), thermodynamically consistent universal interatomic potentials, and a full ImageNet-1k validation re-annotation

entry.title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models

author.name: Pengrui Han, Jacob Andreas, Evelina Fedorenko, Andrea Gregor de Varda

entry.summary: Uses circuit analysis across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains to test whether language models spontaneously develop brain-like functional specialization, and reports that distinct circuits handle language, formal reasoning, social reasoning, and physical reasoning. This is evidence that modularity may be a convergent property of intelligent systems rather than a quirk of biological evolution.

entry.title: AI Research Preference Models

author.name: Thomas Simon Foster, Bassel Al Omari, Tingchen Fu, Thomas Mann, Carl Domond, Lucia Cipolina-Kun, Bhavul Gauri, Muna Aghamelu, Alexander D. Goldie, Eryk Helenowski, Jean-Christophe Gagnon-Audet, Alberto Pepe, Saba Nazir, Daniel Izcovich, Noam Levi, Rishi Hazra, Karen Hambardzumyan, Nicolas Baldwin, Xian Li, Martin Josifoski, Paris Giampouras, Masoud Jalili Sabet, Anya Sims, Hela Momand, Tatiana Shavrina, Despoina Magka, Jason Weston, Yulin Wang, Anirudh Goyal, Jo\~ao Henriques, Yoram Bachrach, Emily McMilin, Jakob Nicolaus Foerster

entry.summary: Tackles the compute bottleneck in autonomous AI research agents, where writing a candidate experiment takes minutes but evaluating it takes hours or days of GPU time, so success depends on how a fixed execution budget is allocated. The authors build research preference models from frozen pretrained language models that predict which candidate solutions are worth actually running, without task-specific training.

entry.title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning

author.name: Kai Chen, Jifeng Ding, Ning Ding, Jiaye Ge, Lixin Gu, Yicheng Gu, Qipeng Guo, Ermo Hua, Haian Huang, Haozheng Hou, Jie Hou, Xiangyu Hong, Che Jiang, Minxi Jin, Cheng Liang, Dahua Lin, Dawei Liu, Kuikun Liu, Chengqi Lv, Haijun Lv, Han Lv, Ningsheng Ma, Biqing Qi, Jianmin Qian, Shiya Su, Youbang Sun, Huanze Tang, Zhongbo Tian, Hanjing Wang, Rui Wang, Ting Wang, Yi Wang, Baiting Wu, Jun Xu, Bowen Yang, Hui Wang, Weida Wang, Haochen Ye, Jiashuo Yu, Shan Yu, Xiaoyi Yu, Qirui Zeng, Qi Zhang, Ming Zhang, Wenwei Zhang, Bowen Zhou, Xinyu Zhou

entry.summary: Intern-S2-Mobius proposes an architecture that separates knowledge storage in a globally shared feed-forward memory from iterative reasoning performed by repeated self-attention operators that query that memory. A 7B model trained from scratch reportedly matches a transformer baseline using about 63 percent of the training data, and a continually pretrained version builds on the existing Qwen3.5-35B model. If it holds up, decoupling knowledge from reasoning is a substantive departure from the standard transformer block.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 15, 2026
entry.summary:
Today's strongest work is empirical measurement of what frontier systems actually deliver and actually do. METR compiles longitudinal public series across cyber vulnerability discovery, mathematical results, and algorithmic optimization to test whether aggregate discovery rates are accelerating — a rare quantitative check on AI-for-science claims. Ecosystem analysis of GLM-5.3 argues Chinese open-weight-bound models are reaching frontier benchmark parity, with implications for release-cadence and cost pressure.

  • Agent reliability: the open LARA testbed shows frontier agents violate legal standards and provider usage policies even when explicitly instructed to comply, across broad model coverage
  • Runtime self-estimation work finds coding agents cannot predict or retrospectively estimate their own wall-clock duration, exposing an unmeasured evaluation axis for scheduling and oversight
  • Interpretability/safety: a toy study tests the widely cited probe-evasion claim, showing optimization pressure can push models to obfuscate a safety-relevant feature from adversarially trained linear probes
  • A research agenda proposes biological foundation models (DNA, protein, gene-expression, cell imaging) as cleaner mechanistic-interpretability testbeds, motivated by biosecurity auditing

Governance and assurance items are more speculative but concrete. A legally grounded catalogue maps US executive branch statutory and unilateral levers over frontier labs; a separate proposal argues for enforcing safety compliance at the GPU/hardware layer to address open-weight cyber misuse. Methodologically, a fine-tuned conceptual reasoning judge targets grading in non-verifiable domains, and a chip/autonomous-vehicle V&V practitioner imports rewind-fix-revalidate discipline into frontier AI assurance.

entry.title: Have We Seen an Acceleration in Discoveries?
entry.summary: METR compiles public data series across cyber vulnerability discovery, mathematical results, and algorithmic optimizations to test whether the aggregate rate of discovery has visibly accelerated, treating early 2026 as a candidate breakpoint. The tentative finding is a sharp acceleration in vulnerability discovery, a modest and hard-to-measure acceleration in math, and no dramatic change in optimization discoveries. The authors caveat that undisclosed internal lab discoveries would not appear in public data.
